title: Revenue Recognition, Billing, and Procurement Playbook
author: Jordan Li
content:
Purpose and scope
-----------------
This playbook documents Redwood Inference's end-to-end procedures for budgeting & forecasting handoffs into procurement, contract lifecycle and legal review, vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition & billing practices. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement approvers, and business owners who enter into supplier or customer agreements.

Scope:
- Applies to all vendor and customer contracts, purchases, and billing arrangements executed by Redwood Inference entities worldwide unless otherwise noted in regional addenda.
- Covers procurement approvals, PO creation, contract review and signature, vendor onboarding, invoice processing, AR aging thresholds, and monthly close evidence for revenue recognition.

Definitions
-----------
- PO: Purchase Order.
- Spend Owner: The business or product owner requesting the purchase.
- Contract Owner: Individual responsible for negotiating and tracking the contract (usually the requester or product manager).
- RevRec: Revenue recognition.
- Deferred Revenue: Payments received but not yet recognized as revenue under accounting rules.
- SaaS ARR: Annualized recurring revenue from hosted or subscription products.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Finance (Revenue & Accounting): Maintain RevRec policy, run month-end close, validate recognized revenue and deferred schedule, produce GL entries.
- Procurement: Manage vendor onboarding, POs, preferred-vendor lists, and procurement system (Coupa).
- Legal: Contract review, templates, risk approval for non-standard terms, and signature authority matrix.
- Sales/Commercial / Partnerships: Negotiate commercial terms, submit contracts to Legal/Finance for review.
- Spend Owner / Requester: Initiates purchase, selects vendor, and provides justification & budget code.

Approval thresholds and routing (quick reference)
------------------------------------------------
| Amount (USD)          | Approver(s)                              | Required Actions / Notes                         |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| $0 - $5,000           | Spend Owner / Department Manager         | Corporate card preferred; receipts uploaded to Concur within 5 business days. |
| $5,001 - $25,000      | Department Head + Procurement             | Create PO in Coupa; Finance notified.           |
| $25,001 - $250,000    | Department Head + Procurement + Finance  | Procurement issues PO; Legal review if contract > 12 months or includes indemnities. |
| $250,001+             | VP Finance (or CFO) + Legal + Procurement | Executive approval required; Legal required for any non-standard clauses. |
| Any spend with customer data processing | Legal + Security (InfoSec)              | Must include Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and Security Questionnaire completed. |

Procurement procedure (step-by-step)
------------------------------------
1. Business case & budget confirmation:
   - Requester verifies budget in the quarterly forecast and obtains department head approval.
   - For new vendors, confirm preferred vendor status or justify single-source selection.
2. Requisition creation (Coupa):
   - Enter vendor, description, GL code, cost center, and contract reference (if exists).
   - Attach quotes and SOWs.
3. Approval routing:
   - Automated routing per thresholds above; manual escalation to Finance for atypical items.
4. PO issuance & vendor notification:
   - Procurement creates PO and sends to vendor with standard terms.
5. Receiving & invoice matching:
   - Requester confirms deliverables or receipt of service in Coupa.
   - AP matches invoice to PO and receipt; discrepancies >5% require dispute and hold.
6. Payment:
   - Standard net-30 unless supplier negotiated otherwise and Finance approves.

Contract and legal process (lifecycle)
------------------------------------
1. Drafting & negotiation:
   - Sales/Buyer drafts commercial term sheet and submits to Legal via contract intake form (Confluence link: /contracts/intake).
   - Legal references master templates stored in the Legal template library. Avoid non-standard redlines without prior Legal approval.
2. Risk triage:
   - Legal assigns low/medium/high risk tags. High-risk items (e.g., extensive indemnities, IP assignment, custom SLAs) escalate to GC and Finance.
3. Signatures:
   - Standard vendor contracts: delegated signature authority per signature matrix.
   - Customer-facing commitments requiring SLA/Security exceptions must be signed by VP of Revenue or CFO.
   - Use DocuSign for electronic signatures.
4. Storage & tracking:
   - Signed contracts uploaded to Contract Repository (ContractSafe) and referenced in Coupa/ERP.

Revenue recognition & billing policies
------------------------------------
- Governing standard: ASC 606 (or IFRS 15 where applicable). Finance owns RevRec policy and will coordinate with external auditors.
- Revenue types and recognition patterns:
  - SaaS subscriptions (hosted API): recognize ratably over the contractual term from service commencement.
  - One-time implementation or professional services: recognize upon completion of deliverables and customer acceptance or per milestone if enforceable.
  - Usage / metered billing: recognize when usage is determinable and invoiced; estimated usage at period-end adjusted in next period.
- Billing cadence & systems:
  - Hosted API customers: automated monthly billing via Stripe (or configured billing platform); invoices generated within 3 business days after cutoff.
  - Enterprise customers on contract: invoice per agreed cadence (monthly/quarterly/annual) via AR team; payment terms typically net-30 unless negotiated.
  - Invoice generation SLO: 95% of invoices generated within 3 business days of billing period close.
- Deferred revenue & cutoffs:
  - Payments received in advance recorded to deferred revenue liability. Monthly close includes a RevRec checklist: verify contract terms, start/end dates, prepaid amounts, and amortization schedules.
- Contract modifications & change orders:
  - Material changes (price/term/volume) require finance re-evaluation for contract modification accounting; document change order and update RevRec schedule.

Accounts receivable & collections
--------------------------------
- AR aging targets:
  - Current (0-30 days): 90%+ goal
  - 31-60 days: <7% target
  - 61-90 days: <2% target
  - >90 days: <1% target; escalated to Finance leadership and Sales for recovery.
- Collections playbook:
  1. Day 1-7: automated payment reminders via billing system.
  2. Day 15: AR specialist email + account owner outreach.
  3. Day 30: formal past-due notice and hold on services for non-contractual customers (subject to contract terms).
  4. >60 days: involve Legal for collections and assess provision for doubtful accounts.

Controls, audit evidence & month-end close checklist
--------------------------------------------------
Monthly close evidence to retain (minimum):
- Signed contracts and amendments for all revenue > $10k recognized in the period.
- Customer invoices and payment confirmations (bank statements or Stripe remittance).
- RevRec schedule exported from ERP showing deferred balances and amortization entries.
- Procurement POs and vendor invoices supporting material purchases recognized as cost of goods sold or capitalized.
- Access logs for Contract Repository and Coupa showing approval flows (for SOX sample testing).

Month-end checklist (Finance owner)
1. Confirm all cut-off invoices are posted and billed.
2. Reconcile deferred revenue roll-forward against contracts.
3. Review any contract modifications and ensure RevRec schedules updated.
4. Produce revenue journal entries and obtain Controller review.
5. Upload supporting evidence to audit folder with index.

Common exceptions & negotiation fallback guidelines
------------------------------------------------
- Non-standard customer requests (custom SLA, refund terms): require Legal + VP Revenue sign-off and explicit RevRec treatment documented; prefer to route these to the Enterprise approvals workflow.
- Vendor requests for accelerated payment or custom T&Cs: Procurement evaluates against preferred supplier terms; exceptions annotated and approved by Finance for material value.

--------------------------------

Contact & escalation
--------------------

- Procurement lead: Priya Singh (procurement@redwood.ai) — procurement system & vendor onboarding.
